title: Localized tensor-Hom evaluation is independent of its chain presentation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and fix a derived category $D$ of its sheaves of modules. Use the tensor and internal-Hom models of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-model] and the explicit uncurrying of [lem-pc-tensor-hom-uncurry-differential]. Let $P,L,M,P',L',M'$ be arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complexes of these module sheaves, with $P,P'$ K-flat. Let $\phi:P\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(M))$ and $\phi':P'\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L',I(M'))$, where $I$ is the fixed functorial K-injective resolution. Suppose $QP=QP'$, $QL=QL'$, $QM=QM'$ as literal objects of $D$, and the normalized inputs $Q\phi\circ\rho_{L,M}^{-1}$ and $Q\phi'\circ\rho_{L',M'}^{-1}$ are equal after transport by these equalities. Then the morphisms obtained by composing the tensor model comparison, the localized explicit uncurrying and the inverse resolution augmentation are equal after the same equality transport. The Lean statement uses heterogeneous equality for these transported equalities. No extension to other derived inputs, and no family of functions, is asserted.

proof.text: Specialize localized chain-map evaluation naturality with source the Hom complex, its input the identity, source-variable map phi, and identity maps in L and M. Functor preservation of identities simplifies the resulting input to phi. Tensor composition and the inverse-hom equation for the internal-Hom resolution isomorphism factor the evaluation through the normalized input tensor identity followed by normalized identity evaluation. No K-flatness is needed for this factorization.
Apply identity-evaluation coherence to the literal equalities QL=QLprime and QM=QMprime. This compares only the fixed evaluation morphisms, independently of P and phi.

Equality induction on QP=QPprime, QL=QLprime and QM=QMprime puts the normalized inputs and identity evaluations in the same Hom sets. Convert their heterogeneous equalities to equalities, substitute, and conclude heterogeneous equality of the tensor-composites. Rewrite both factorization equations to obtain the original conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08DJ, 0A90, 0A96. The restored Sheaf module publicly re-exports the upstream theorem with the same acyclic-tensor K-flatness definition under its canonical name IsKFlatTensor. Its proved argument is still normalized-input factorization and identity-evaluation coherence.

theorem tensorHomUncurry_representative_coherence (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (P L M P' L' M' : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (hP' : P'.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat)
    (φ : P ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf) L
      ((schemeHomKInjectiveResolution X).obj M))
    (φ' : P' ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf) L'
      ((schemeHomKInjectiveResolution X).obj M'))
    (hK : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P = DerivedCategory.Q.obj P')
    (hL : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L = DerivedCategory.Q.obj L')
    (hM : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M = DerivedCategory.Q.obj M')
    (hφ : HEq (DerivedCategory.Q.map φ ≫
        (schemeDerivedInternalHomResolutionIso X L M).inv)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.map φ' ≫
        (schemeDerivedInternalHomResolutionIso X L' M').inv)) :
    HEq (pullbackTensorModelMap X P L ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (schemeTensorHomUncurry X P L M φ) ≫
          schemeHomResolutionInverse X M)
      (pullbackTensorModelMap X P' L' ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (schemeTensorHomUncurry X P' L' M' φ') ≫
          schemeHomResolutionInverse X M')
